$comment: Finding texts (REQUIREMENTS #560): the WHAT / HOW / compliance / MITRE texts of SI's own Risk Analysis reports as DATA, filled into the generic SI finding fields (si_description, si_remediation, si_fix_remediation (how to fix, REQUIREMENTS #590), si_remediation_type, si_reference_url, si_compliance_tags, si_mitre_tactics, si_mitre_techniques) -- no longer fixed text in the report YAML or keyword tables in the engine. reports: one item per report (id = ReportName); source = report (SI's own finding: these texts are the finding's) | provider (the rows carry their source's own texts -- Defender, Defender for Cloud -- and these only fill what the source left empty). A field an item does not hold stays unknown (si_remediation: written by Invardia or the customer). inference: the keyword rows that derive MITRE and compliance references for a row whose report and source say nothing (first match over SecurityDomain + Subcategory + ConfigurationName, then the security domain's default). rowColumns: which Risk Analysis row column fills which SI finding field (first non-empty). Customer changes: Pro = one cfg.ItemOverride per report (finding-texts:<report> -- override or add); Community = finding-texts.custom.json, per id. engine/data-model/SI-FindingTexts.ps1.

reports.si_description: Applications (service principals) the Exposure Graph says can impersonate users, with the tier and asset risk factors of the users they can act as (the CI).

reports.si_description: Applications (service principals) the Exposure Graph says can impersonate users, with the tier and asset risk factors of the users they can act as (the CI).

reports.si_description: Workloads that sign in as a managed identity which holds a role or permission on an Azure resource -- whoever runs code on the workload reaches the resource -- with the tier of the resource reached (the CI).

reports.si_fix_remediation: Give the managed identity only the roles the workload needs, on the narrowest scope; protect the workload as the tier of what its identity reaches (patching, access to the workload, no interactive sign-in).
reports.si_description: Workloads that sign in as a managed identity which holds a role or permission on an Azure resource -- whoever runs code on the workload reaches the resource -- with the tier of the resource reached (the CI).

reports.si_fix_remediation: Give sign-in and administration rights on Tier 0 servers only to Tier 0 administration accounts; remove the role from the user or the group, or move the group's members to the server's tier.
reports.si_description: Users below Tier 0 who are entitled (directly or through a group) to sign in to or administer a Tier 0 server -- the entitlement, not the logon events.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Give sign-in and administration rights on Tier 0 servers only to Tier 0 administration accounts; remove the role from the user or the group, or move the group's members to the server's tier.
reports.si_description: Users below Tier 0 who are entitled (directly or through a group) to sign in to or administer a Tier 0 server -- the entitlement, not the logon events.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Remove owners who are not administrators of the application's tier, or move the ownership to a Tier 0 / Tier 1 administration account; owners can add credentials to the application.
reports.si_description: Tier 0 and Tier 1 service principals owned by accounts on a less critical tier -- an owner can add a credential and sign in as the application.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Remove owners who are not administrators of the application's tier, or move the ownership to a Tier 0 / Tier 1 administration account; owners can add credentials to the application.
reports.si_description: Tier 0 and Tier 1 service principals owned by accounts on a less critical tier -- an owner can add a credential and sign in as the application.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Register the user for multifactor authentication (phishing-resistant methods preferred) and require it with a Conditional Access policy that covers all users.
reports.si_description: All enabled users with no MFA registration, across all tiers. Excludes accounts created within the last 7 days. Severity scales with tier.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Confirm with the manager whether the account is still needed; disable it if not, and delete it after your retention period. Recurring access reviews catch inactive accounts automatically.
reports.si_description: Enabled user accounts with no interactive or non-interactive sign-in for 180+ days. Excludes guest/B2B accounts (handled separately). Stale privileged accounts are particularly dangerous as they may be forgotten but still retain active permissions.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Confirm with the manager whether the account is still needed; disable it if not, and delete it after your retention period. Recurring access reviews catch inactive accounts automatically.
reports.si_description: Per-user detail for enabled accounts with no sign-in for 180+ days. Excludes guest/B2B. Includes last sign-in dates, role details, and tier.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Remove the guest account, or disable it until its sponsor confirms it is needed, and run recurring access reviews for guest users.
reports.si_description: B2B guest/external collaborator accounts with no sign-in for 90+ days. Guests have a shorter stale threshold than internal users as they represent external access that should be regularly re-validated. Stale guest accounts are a common vector for supply chain and partner-related compromises.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Confirm the application is still used; if not, remove its privileged permissions and credentials and delete the service principal. If it is used, find out why it has not signed in.
reports.si_description: Service Principals and Managed Identities with Tier 0/1 permissions (high-privilege app roles or directory roles) that have not authenticated for 180+ days. Dormant privileged workload identities are attractive targets as they may retain permissions long after the business use case has ended.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Confirm the application is still used; if not, remove its privileged permissions and credentials and delete the service principal. If it is used, find out why it has not signed in.
reports.si_description: Per-SPN/MI detail for privileged workloads inactive for 180+ days. Includes permission details, credential info, and owner status.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Rotate the credential before it expires: add a new certificate or secret, update the application that uses it, then remove the old one. Prefer certificates or managed identities over client secrets.
reports.si_description: Service Principals with client secrets or certificates that have expired or will expire within 30 days. Expired credentials cause service outages. Credentials expiring on privileged SPNs are especially urgent as emergency secret rotation under pressure increases risk of mistakes or insecure handling.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Assign at least two owners who answer for the application (credential rotation, permission review), or remove the service principal if no one claims it.
reports.si_description: Service Principals with no registered owner. Ownerless SPNs have no accountability for credential rotation, permission review, or decommissioning. Privileged orphaned SPNs are critical: no one is responsible for monitoring or revoking access.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Convert the permanent (active) role assignment to an eligible assignment in Privileged Identity Management, with MFA, justification and a time limit on activation.
reports.si_description: Privileged users with permanent (non-PIM) role assignments. Best practice requires all Tier 0/1 roles to be assigned via PIM (just-in-time) to reduce the standing attack surface. Permanent assignments mean the role is always active, even when not in use, providing a persistent target for attackers.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Remove the account from the on-premises privileged group (including nested membership); if the access is needed, document it and manage it through your privileged access process.
reports.si_description: Users classified as shadow admins: they hold Tier 0/1 AD group membership (e.g. Domain Admins inherited via group nesting) but have no visible Entra ID role assignments. These accounts exercise privileged AD access that may not be tracked by standard Entra ID governance tooling, creating a blind spot in access reviews and PIM coverage.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Remove the password-never-expires setting from the privileged account, rotate its password and move it to passwordless or phishing-resistant MFA sign-in.
reports.si_description: Privileged accounts with password-never-expires flag set. While passwordless and MFA mitigate this, a non-expiring password on a privileged account means a compromised credential remains valid indefinitely. Combined with no MFA or stale sign-in, this represents a critical unmanaged risk.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Review the multi-tenant application's permissions: remove the Tier 0/1 permissions it does not need or make it single-tenant, and revoke consent if the publisher is not trusted.
reports.si_description: Multi-tenant service principals (accessible from external tenants) with Tier 0/1 permissions. Multi-tenant apps expose credentials and permissions to external party control. If a partner tenant is compromised, the SPN can be leveraged to attack your tenant with full privileges.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Remove the privileged role from the external or guest account; if the person needs admin access, give them a member account in this tenant governed by PIM.
reports.si_description: External/B2B guest users with Tier 0/1 Entra ID roles. External identities should never hold privileged directory roles. Their accounts are governed by their home tenant's security posture which may be significantly lower than yours. A compromised partner account with Global Admin in your tenant is a catastrophic risk.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Rotate the privileged account's password now and move the account to passwordless or phishing-resistant MFA sign-in.
reports.si_description: Privileged accounts whose password has not been changed in over 365 days. Long-lived passwords increase the window of exploitation if credentials were exposed in a breach that was never detected. Applies to accounts where password authentication is still a factor (non-passwordless-only accounts).

reports.si_fix_remediation: Limit the application's mail access to the mailboxes it needs (Exchange application access policy or RBAC for Applications), or remove the mail permission if it is not used.
reports.si_description: Service Principals with mailbox-level Microsoft Graph permissions (Mail.ReadWrite, Mail.Send, MailboxSettings.ReadWrite or equivalent). These permissions allow an app to read all email in the organisation or send as any user - a high-value target for data exfiltration and business email compromise (BEC). SPNs with mailbox access and no active usage are especially concerning.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Investigate the account in Microsoft Defender for Identity: review its risk signals, reset its credentials and revoke sessions if compromise is suspected, and confirm its privileged access is still required.
reports.si_description: Identities flagged by Microsoft Defender for Identity as high or critical risk, cross-referenced with our asset tier classification. MDI risk signals include observed lateral movement, credential exposure, anomalous behaviour, and UEBA scoring. When a Tier 0/1 identity has elevated MDI risk, it indicates an active or recent threat that requires immediate investigation.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Verify the sign-ins with the user; if they are not expected, revoke sessions and reset credentials. Limit privileged sign-ins to trusted locations or compliant devices with Conditional Access.
reports.si_description: Privileged users (Tier 0/1) who have successfully signed in from a network location that is NOT defined as a trusted named location in Conditional Access. Admin accounts should only authenticate from managed, trusted networks (corporate VPN, PAW networks, known office IPs). Sign-in from an untrusted location on a privileged account is a strong indicator of credential compromise, policy bypass, or an admin using personal devices/networks for privileged tasks. Severity: Very High (fixed).

reports.si_fix_remediation: Verify the sign-ins with the user; if they are not expected, revoke sessions and reset credentials. Limit privileged sign-ins to trusted locations or compliant devices with Conditional Access.
reports.si_description: Per-user detail: privileged accounts with non-trusted location sign-ins. Shows sign-in count, IPs, countries, and last occurrence.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Verify the sign-ins; limit the service account to trusted locations with Conditional Access and rotate its credentials if the sign-ins are unexplained.
reports.si_description: Accounts classified as service accounts by MDI (MDI_IsServiceAccount = true) that have successfully authenticated from non-trusted network locations. Service accounts are expected to authenticate exclusively from known, trusted infrastructure (application servers, automation agents). Authentication from an untrusted location strongly suggests the service account credentials have been harvested and are being used by a threat actor. Severity: High (fixed).

reports.si_fix_remediation: Confirm the break-glass sign-in was a genuine emergency; if not, handle it as a security incident. Rotate the account's credentials after any use.
reports.si_description: Any successful sign-in by an account flagged as a break-glass emergency account. Break-glass accounts are only valid for use during genuine catastrophic failures where normal admin access is unavailable. Every sign-in by a break-glass account must be investigated to confirm it was authorised and justified. This is an operational alert that should trigger an immediate review process. Severity: Very High (fixed) -- all break-glass usage is critical regardless of context.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Remove RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory from the application unless it is a governed role-management tool; grant a narrower permission instead.
reports.si_description: Service Principals with the RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory Graph permission. This permission allows the SPN to assign ANY Entra ID role to ANY principal, including Global Administrator. A compromised SPN with this permission can immediately elevate any account to full tenant administrator -- the equivalent of a skeleton key to the entire Entra ID tenant. This is arguably the most dangerous single Graph permission that exists. Severity: Very High (fixed).

reports.si_fix_remediation: Remove AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All from the application unless it is required: it lets the application grant itself any permission.
reports.si_description: Service Principals with AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All permission. This allows the SPN to grant any Graph application permission to any other SPN, including granting itself Global Admin-equivalent permissions such as RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory or Directory.ReadWrite.All. A compromised SPN with this permission can bootstrap full tenant takeover in two API calls: grant itself dangerous permissions, then use them. Severity: Very High (fixed).

reports.si_fix_remediation: Remove PrivilegedAccess.ReadWrite.AzureAD from the application unless it is a governed PIM management tool.
reports.si_description: Service Principals with PrivilegedAccess.ReadWrite.AzureAD permission. This allows the SPN to directly create, modify, or remove PIM role eligibility and assignment schedules. A compromised SPN with this permission can make any account permanently eligible for Global Administrator with no approval workflow, or remove existing PIM assignments to cover tracks. Severity: Very High (fixed) -- direct PIM manipulation capability.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Confirm where the application comes from; remove its high permissions (or the application) if it is not trusted, and require a verified publisher for applications that get Tier 0/1 permissions.
reports.si_description: Service Principals with Tier 0/1 permissions whose publisher has not been verified by Microsoft. Unverified publishers are anonymous -- there is no accountability for the code running in your tenant. High-privilege unverified apps represent a supply chain risk: the app developer could push malicious updates, and there is no way to validate the publisher's identity or intent. Severity: High (fixed).

reports.si_fix_remediation: Verify the new account and its Tier 0 role with the person who assigned it; if it is not authorised, remove the role, disable the account and investigate.
reports.si_description: User accounts created within the last 24 hours that already have a Tier 0 Entra ID role assigned. In a healthy environment, newly created accounts go through a provisioning workflow and role assignments require approval. Immediate Tier 0 role on a brand-new account indicates either a provisioning process bypass, a compromised privileged account creating rogue admin accounts, or a misconfigured automation script with excessive initial permissions. Severity: Very High (fixed) -- immediate Tier 0 access on new account.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Remove the eligible and active PIM role assignments from the disabled account (part of the leaver process).
reports.si_description: Disabled user accounts that still have PIM eligible role assignments active. When an account is disabled (e.g. employee leaving), all role assignments should be removed as part of the offboarding process. An eligible assignment on a disabled account means the account could be re-enabled and immediately used to activate privileged access -- a common post-compromise technique. Severity: High (fixed).

reports.si_fix_remediation: Stop interactive use of the service account: block interactive sign-in (Conditional Access or logon rights), rotate its password and give the person a personal account.
reports.si_description: Accounts classified by MDI as service accounts (MDI_IsServiceAccount = true) that have interactive human sign-ins recorded in SigninLogs. Service accounts should authenticate exclusively via non-interactive flows (daemon credentials, managed identity, service principal). Interactive logins indicate the service account credentials are being used by a human -- either a shared password problem, a developer using service credentials to bypass controls, or a threat actor who harvested the credentials and is performing hands-on-keyboard activity. Severity: High (fixed).

reports.si_fix_remediation: Investigate the account in Microsoft Defender for Identity (its alerts and unusual activities); reset its credentials and revoke sessions if compromise is suspected.
reports.si_description: Active accounts with MDI Investigation Priority Percentile in the top 10% (MDI_InvestigationPriorityPct >= 90). MDI calculates this score based on observed anomalous behaviours, lateral movement signals, unusual access patterns, and UEBA risk scoring. A high investigation priority means MDI has observed behaviour that warrants review. When this is combined with a privileged identity, it represents a potentially active threat that requires immediate attention. Severity: High (fixed).

reports.si_fix_remediation: Replace the synchronised admin account with a cloud-only admin account, and remove privileged Entra roles from synchronised accounts.
reports.si_description: Privileged admin accounts (Tier 0/1) that are synchronised from on-premises AD rather than being cloud-only. Admin accounts should be cloud-native to avoid on-prem compromise pivoting to cloud. A compromised AD environment (e.g. via ransomware) can directly take over cloud admin accounts that are synced from AD. Severity: Very High - on-prem sync of privileged accounts breaks cloud/AD separation.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Confirm whether the privileged account is needed; if not, remove its roles and disable it. If it is needed, make the role eligible in PIM instead of permanent.
reports.si_description: Privileged accounts (Tier 0/1) created more than 14 days ago that have never signed in. Unused privileged accounts represent dormant attack surface - they hold permissions but have no operational owner actively monitoring them. Common cause: accounts created for a project that never started, or provisioned for a consultant who never onboarded. Severity: High (fixed).

reports.si_fix_remediation: Reduce Global Administrators to the few who need it (Microsoft recommends fewer than five, plus break-glass accounts): move the others to least-privilege roles and make Global Administrator eligible in PIM.
reports.si_description: Detects when the organisation has more than 5 active Global Administrator accounts. Microsoft recommends 2-5 Global Admins maximum. Each additional Global Admin increases the attack surface proportionally. Organisations with 10+ Global Admins typically have role assignment hygiene problems and lack a formal review process. Severity: High (fixed) - excessive Global Admin count is always a significant risk.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Review the break-glass account's use: confirm any recent use was an emergency, rotate its credentials after use, and test the account on a schedule so it is known to work.
reports.si_description: Break-glass emergency access accounts with anomalous sign-in patterns. Detects two opposite problems: (1) Break-glass account used recently (< 30 days) WITHOUT an incident - possible misuse (2) Break-glass account has never been tested OR last test was > 180 days ago Break-glass accounts should only be used in genuine emergencies and tested periodically. Severity: Very High (fixed) - any break-glass anomaly is a critical governance failure.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Remove the eligible role assignment the person has never activated, or confirm with them that it is still needed.
reports.si_description: Users with PIM-eligible Tier 0/1 role assignments that have never been activated (no interactive sign-in with the role active). Eligible roles that are never used suggest the assignment is unnecessary and should be removed to reduce blast radius. This also applies to identities with eligible roles but no sign-in at all. Severity: Medium (fixed) - eligible roles are safer than permanent but unused assignments still represent unnecessary standing access that should be cleaned up.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Remove the permanent assignment and keep only the eligible (PIM) assignment of the same role.
reports.si_description: Users who have the same Entra ID role assigned both permanently AND as PIM eligible. This is a misconfiguration: the permanent assignment makes the PIM eligible one redundant and indicates the PIM policy was not followed. The permanent assignment should be removed and only the PIM eligible retained. Severity: Medium-High (fixed) - redundant permanent assignment defeats PIM purpose.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Remove the credential the application does not use; keep one (a certificate preferred) and rotate it on a schedule.
reports.si_description: Service Principals that have both a client secret AND a certificate registered. Over-credentialed SPNs increase the credential attack surface - two different authentication paths must both be managed and rotated. Often indicates legacy credentials were not cleaned up when the SPN was migrated to certificate auth. Severity: Medium (fixed).

reports.si_fix_remediation: Install the security updates on the device and stop privileged sign-ins to it: do admin work from a privileged access workstation.
reports.si_description: Privileged users (permanent or PIM-eligible Tier 0/1 roles) who are observed authenticating to devices that have high or critical severity CVEs outstanding. When an admin logs on to a vulnerable device, their privileged token/credential is exposed on that device. An attacker who exploits the CVE could harvest the admin credential via memory dumps, token theft, or keylogging. Severity: Very High (fixed) - privileged credential exposure on vulnerable device.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Install the security updates on the device and stop privileged sign-ins to it: do admin work from a privileged access workstation.
reports.si_description: Per-pair detail: privileged admin and the specific vulnerable device they can authenticate to. Includes CVE score, internet exposure and device risk.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Stop privileged sign-ins to internet-exposed devices: do admin work from a privileged access workstation or jump host and restrict admin logon rights on exposed servers.
reports.si_description: Privileged users (Tier 0/1) authenticated to internet-facing devices. Privileged sessions should never occur on internet-exposed assets as these devices have a significantly higher chance of being compromised remotely. Even without CVEs, internet-exposed devices face constant attack attempts. An attacker who breaches an internet-exposed device gains access to any privileged credential or token present on that device. Severity: High (fixed).

reports.si_fix_remediation: Keep Tier 0 accounts on Tier 0 devices (privileged access workstations): deny their logon to lower-tier devices with authentication policies or user rights assignment.
reports.si_description: Tier 0 privileged users (Global Admin, Domain Admin etc) authenticating to devices that are NOT classified as Tier 0 assets. Tier 0 admins should only use Tier 0 Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs). Logging on to a standard workstation, developer machine, or shared device exposes Tier 0 credentials to a device with a broader attack surface and potentially lower security controls. Severity: Very High (fixed) - Tier 0 admin on non-PAW device is a tiering violation.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Install the security updates for the exploitable vulnerabilities on the device, and have the PIM-eligible admin use a privileged access workstation for admin work.
reports.si_description: Users with PIM-eligible Tier 0/1 roles authenticated to devices that have vulnerabilities with known exploits available (isExploitVerified or isInExploitKit). Even if the PIM role is not currently activated, the credential harvested from an exploitable device could be used to activate PIM and gain full admin access. Severity: Very High (fixed) - eligible admin credential on actively exploitable device.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Confirm whether the privileged account is needed; if not, remove its roles and disable it. If it is needed, make the role eligible in PIM instead of permanent.
reports.si_description: Per-row detail view for Identity_AdminAccount_NeverUsed_Summary. Privileged accounts (Tier 0/1) created more than 14 days ago that have never signed in. Unused privileged accounts represent dormant attack surface - they hold permissions but have no operational owner actively monitoring them. Common cause: accounts created for a project that never started, or provisioned for a consultant who never onboarded. Severity: High (fixed). Detailed emits one row per affected asset (PrimaryEntityId-keyed), suitable for ticket creation, remediation tracking, and per-asset evidence. Per-identity detail view for AdminAccount NeverUsed Summary.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Replace the synchronised admin account with a cloud-only admin account, and remove privileged Entra roles from synchronised accounts.
reports.si_description: Per-row detail view for Identity_AdminAccount_OnPremSynced_Summary. Privileged admin accounts (Tier 0/1) that are synchronised from on-premises AD rather than being cloud-only. Admin accounts should be cloud-native to avoid on-prem compromise pivoting to cloud. A compromised AD environment (e.g. via ransomware) can directly take over cloud admin accounts that are synced from AD. Severity: Very High - on-prem sync of privileged accounts breaks cloud/AD separation. Detailed emits one row per affected asset (PrimaryEntityId-keyed), suitable for ticket creation, remediation tracking, and per-asset evidence. Per-identity detail view for AdminAccount OnPremisesSyncEnabled Summary.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Stop privileged sign-ins to internet-exposed devices: do admin work from a privileged access workstation or jump host and restrict admin logon rights on exposed servers.
reports.si_description: Per-row detail view for Identity_Admin_LogonTo_InternetExposedDevice_Summary. Privileged users (Tier 0/1) authenticated to internet-facing devices. Privileged sessions should never occur on internet-exposed assets as these devices have a significantly higher chance of being compromised remotely. Even without CVEs, internet-exposed devices face constant attack attempts. An attacker who breaches an internet-exposed device gains access to any privileged credential or token present on that device. Severity: High (fixed). Detailed emits one row per affected asset (PrimaryEntityId-keyed), suitable for ticket creation, remediation tracking, and per-asset evidence. Per-identity detail view for Admin LogonTo InternetExposedDevice Summary.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Keep Tier 0 accounts on Tier 0 devices (privileged access workstations): deny their logon to lower-tier devices with authentication policies or user rights assignment.
reports.si_description: Per-row detail view for Identity_Admin_LogonTo_LowTierDevice_Summary. Tier 0 privileged users (Global Admin, Domain Admin etc) authenticating to devices that are NOT classified as Tier 0 assets. Tier 0 admins should only use Tier 0 Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs). Logging on to a standard workstation, developer machine, or shared device exposes Tier 0 credentials to a device with a broader attack surface and potentially lower security controls. Severity: Very High (fixed) - Tier 0 admin on non-PAW device is a tiering violation. Detailed emits one row per affected asset (PrimaryEntityId-keyed), suitable for ticket creation, remediation tracking, and per-asset evidence. Per-identity detail view for Admin LogonTo LowTierDevice Summary.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Register the user for multifactor authentication (phishing-resistant methods preferred) and require it with a Conditional Access policy that covers all users.
reports.si_description: Per-row detail view for Identity_AnyUser_NoMFA_Summary. All enabled users with no MFA registration, across all tiers. Excludes accounts created within the last 7 days. Severity scales with tier. Detailed emits one row per affected asset (PrimaryEntityId-keyed), suitable for ticket creation, remediation tracking, and per-asset evidence. Per-identity detail view for AnyUser NoMFA Summary.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Review the break-glass account's use: confirm any recent use was an emergency, rotate its credentials after use, and test the account on a schedule so it is known to work.
reports.si_description: Per-row detail view for Identity_BreakGlass_Anomaly_Summary. Break-glass emergency access accounts with anomalous sign-in patterns. Detects two opposite problems: (1) Break-glass account used recently (< 30 days) WITHOUT an incident - possible misuse (2) Break-glass account has never been tested OR last test was > 180 days ago Break-glass accounts should only be used in genuine emergencies and tested periodically. Severity: Very High (fixed) - any break-glass anomaly is a critical governance failure. Detailed emits one row per affected asset (PrimaryEntityId-keyed), suitable for ticket creation, remediation tracking, and per-asset evidence. Per-identity detail view for BreakGlass Anomaly Summary.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Confirm the break-glass sign-in was a genuine emergency; if not, handle it as a security incident. Rotate the account's credentials after any use.
reports.si_description: Per-row detail view for Identity_BreakGlass_SignIn_Detected_Summary. Any successful sign-in by an account flagged as a break-glass emergency account. Break-glass accounts are only valid for use during genuine catastrophic failures where normal admin access is unavailable. Every sign-in by a break-glass account must be investigated to confirm it was authorised and justified. This is an operational alert that should trigger an immediate review process. Severity: Very High (fixed) -- all break-glass usage is critical regardless of context. Detailed emits one row per affected asset (PrimaryEntityId-keyed), suitable for ticket creation, remediation tracking, and per-asset evidence. Per-identity detail view for BreakGlass SignIn Detected Summary.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Remove the eligible and active PIM role assignments from the disabled account (part of the leaver process).
reports.si_description: Per-row detail view for Identity_DisabledAccount_ActivePIMAssignment_Summary. Disabled user accounts that still have PIM eligible role assignments active. When an account is disabled (e.g. employee leaving), all role assignments should be removed as part of the offboarding process. An eligible assignment on a disabled account means the account could be re-enabled and immediately used to activate privileged access -- a common post-compromise technique. Severity: High (fixed). Detailed emits one row per affected asset (PrimaryEntityId-keyed), suitable for ticket creation, remediation tracking, and per-asset evidence. Per-identity detail view for DisabledAccount ActivePIMAssignment Summary.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Install the security updates for the exploitable vulnerabilities on the device, and have the PIM-eligible admin use a privileged access workstation for admin work.
reports.si_description: Per-row detail view for Identity_EligibleAdmin_LogonTo_ExploitableDevice_Summary. Users with PIM-eligible Tier 0/1 roles authenticated to devices that have vulnerabilities with known exploits available (isExploitVerified or isInExploitKit). Even if the PIM role is not currently activated, the credential harvested from an exploitable device could be used to activate PIM and gain full admin access. Severity: Very High (fixed) - eligible admin credential on actively exploitable device. Detailed emits one row per affected asset (PrimaryEntityId-keyed), suitable for ticket creation, remediation tracking, and per-asset evidence. Per-identity detail view for EligibleAdmin LogonTo ExploitableDevice Summary.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Remove the privileged role from the external or guest account; if the person needs admin access, give them a member account in this tenant governed by PIM.
reports.si_description: Per-row detail view for Identity_ExternalUser_PrivilegedRole_Summary. External/B2B guest users with Tier 0/1 Entra ID roles. External identities should never hold privileged directory roles. Their accounts are governed by their home tenant's security posture which may be significantly lower than yours. A compromised partner account with Global Admin in your tenant is a catastrophic risk. Detailed emits one row per affected asset (PrimaryEntityId-keyed), suitable for ticket creation, remediation tracking, and per-asset evidence. Per-identity detail view for ExternalUser PrivilegedRole Summary.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Investigate the account in Microsoft Defender for Identity (its alerts and unusual activities); reset its credentials and revoke sessions if compromise is suspected.
reports.si_description: Per-row detail view for Identity_HighMDIInvestigationPriority_Summary. Active accounts with MDI Investigation Priority Percentile in the top 10% (MDI_InvestigationPriorityPct >= 90). MDI calculates this score based on observed anomalous behaviours, lateral movement signals, unusual access patterns, and UEBA risk scoring. A high investigation priority means MDI has observed behaviour that warrants review. When this is combined with a privileged identity, it represents a potentially active threat that requires immediate attention. Severity: High (fixed). Detailed emits one row per affected asset (PrimaryEntityId-keyed), suitable for ticket creation, remediation tracking, and per-asset evidence. Per-identity detail view for HighMDIInvestigationPriority Summary.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Investigate the account in Microsoft Defender for Identity: review its risk signals, reset its credentials and revoke sessions if compromise is suspected, and confirm its privileged access is still required.
reports.si_description: Per-row detail view for Identity_HighValueTarget_MDIRisk_Summary. Identities flagged by Microsoft Defender for Identity as high or critical risk, cross-referenced with our asset tier classification. MDI risk signals include observed lateral movement, credential exposure, anomalous behaviour, and UEBA scoring. When a Tier 0/1 identity has elevated MDI risk, it indicates an active or recent threat that requires immediate investigation. Detailed emits one row per affected asset (PrimaryEntityId-keyed), suitable for ticket creation, remediation tracking, and per-asset evidence. Per-identity detail view for HighValueTarget MDIRisk Summary.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Review the multi-tenant application's permissions: remove the Tier 0/1 permissions it does not need or make it single-tenant, and revoke consent if the publisher is not trusted.
reports.si_description: Per-row detail view for Identity_MultiTenant_HighPermission_SPN_Summary. Multi-tenant service principals (accessible from external tenants) with Tier 0/1 permissions. Multi-tenant apps expose credentials and permissions to external party control. If a partner tenant is compromised, the SPN can be leveraged to attack your tenant with full privileges. Detailed emits one row per affected asset (PrimaryEntityId-keyed), suitable for ticket creation, remediation tracking, and per-asset evidence. Per-identity detail view for MultiTenant HighPermission SPN Summary.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Verify the new account and its Tier 0 role with the person who assigned it; if it is not authorised, remove the role, disable the account and investigate.
reports.si_description: Per-row detail view for Identity_NewAccount_ImmediateTier0Role_Summary. User accounts created within the last 24 hours that already have a Tier 0 Entra ID role assigned. In a healthy environment, newly created accounts go through a provisioning workflow and role assignments require approval. Immediate Tier 0 role on a brand-new account indicates either a provisioning process bypass, a compromised privileged account creating rogue admin accounts, or a misconfigured automation script with excessive initial permissions. Severity: Very High (fixed) -- immediate Tier 0 access on new account. Detailed emits one row per affected asset (PrimaryEntityId-keyed), suitable for ticket creation, remediation tracking, and per-asset evidence. Per-identity detail view for NewAccount ImmediateTier0Role Summary.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Remove the permanent assignment and keep only the eligible (PIM) assignment of the same role.
reports.si_description: Per-row detail view for Identity_PIM_DuplicateRoleAssignment_Summary. Users who have the same Entra ID role assigned both permanently AND as PIM eligible. This is a misconfiguration: the permanent assignment makes the PIM eligible one redundant and indicates the PIM policy was not followed. The permanent assignment should be removed and only the PIM eligible retained. Severity: Medium-High (fixed) - redundant permanent assignment defeats PIM purpose. Detailed emits one row per affected asset (PrimaryEntityId-keyed), suitable for ticket creation, remediation tracking, and per-asset evidence. Per-identity detail view for PIM DuplicateRoleAssignment Summary.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Remove the eligible role assignment the person has never activated, or confirm with them that it is still needed.
reports.si_description: Per-row detail view for Identity_PIM_EligibleNeverActivated_Summary. Users with PIM-eligible Tier 0/1 role assignments that have never been activated (no interactive sign-in with the role active). Eligible roles that are never used suggest the assignment is unnecessary and should be removed to reduce blast radius. This also applies to identities with eligible roles but no sign-in at all. Severity: Medium (fixed) - eligible roles are safer than permanent but unused assignments still represent unnecessary standing access that should be cleaned up. Detailed emits one row per affected asset (PrimaryEntityId-keyed), suitable for ticket creation, remediation tracking, and per-asset evidence. Per-identity detail view for PIM EligibleNeverActivated Summary.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Remove the password-never-expires setting from the privileged account, rotate its password and move it to passwordless or phishing-resistant MFA sign-in.
reports.si_description: Per-row detail view for Identity_PasswordNeverExpires_Privileged_Summary. Privileged accounts with password-never-expires flag set. While passwordless and MFA mitigate this, a non-expiring password on a privileged account means a compromised credential remains valid indefinitely. Combined with no MFA or stale sign-in, this represents a critical unmanaged risk. Detailed emits one row per affected asset (PrimaryEntityId-keyed), suitable for ticket creation, remediation tracking, and per-asset evidence. Per-identity detail view for PasswordNeverExpires Privileged Summary.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Convert the permanent (active) role assignment to an eligible assignment in Privileged Identity Management, with MFA, justification and a time limit on activation.
reports.si_description: Per-row detail view for Identity_PermanentPrivilegedRole_Summary. Privileged users with permanent (non-PIM) role assignments. Best practice requires all Tier 0/1 roles to be assigned via PIM (just-in-time) to reduce the standing attack surface. Permanent assignments mean the role is always active, even when not in use, providing a persistent target for attackers. Detailed emits one row per affected asset (PrimaryEntityId-keyed), suitable for ticket creation, remediation tracking, and per-asset evidence. Per-identity detail view for PermanentPrivilegedRole Summary.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Rotate the privileged account's password now and move the account to passwordless or phishing-resistant MFA sign-in.
reports.si_description: Per-row detail view for Identity_PrivilegedUser_StalePassword_Summary. Privileged accounts whose password has not been changed in over 365 days. Long-lived passwords increase the window of exploitation if credentials were exposed in a breach that was never detected. Applies to accounts where password authentication is still a factor (non-passwordless-only accounts). Detailed emits one row per affected asset (PrimaryEntityId-keyed), suitable for ticket creation, remediation tracking, and per-asset evidence. Per-identity detail view for PrivilegedUser StalePassword Summary.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Remove AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All from the application unless it is required: it lets the application grant itself any permission.
reports.si_description: Per-row detail view for Identity_SPN_AppRoleAssignmentWrite_Summary. Service Principals with AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All permission. This allows the SPN to grant any Graph application permission to any other SPN, including granting itself Global Admin-equivalent permissions such as RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory or Directory.ReadWrite.All. A compromised SPN with this permission can bootstrap full tenant takeover in two API calls: grant itself dangerous permissions, then use them. Severity: Very High (fixed). Detailed emits one row per affected asset (PrimaryEntityId-keyed), suitable for ticket creation, remediation tracking, and per-asset evidence. Per-identity detail view for SPN AppRoleAssignmentWrite Summary.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Rotate the credential before it expires: add a new certificate or secret, update the application that uses it, then remove the old one. Prefer certificates or managed identities over client secrets.
reports.si_description: Per-row detail view for Identity_SPN_ExpiringCredentials_Summary. Service Principals with client secrets or certificates that have expired or will expire within 30 days. Expired credentials cause service outages. Credentials expiring on privileged SPNs are especially urgent as emergency secret rotation under pressure increases risk of mistakes or insecure handling. Detailed emits one row per affected asset (PrimaryEntityId-keyed), suitable for ticket creation, remediation tracking, and per-asset evidence. Per-identity detail view for SPN ExpiringCredentials Summary.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Limit the application's mail access to the mailboxes it needs (Exchange application access policy or RBAC for Applications), or remove the mail permission if it is not used.
reports.si_description: Per-row detail view for Identity_SPN_MailboxAccess_Summary. Service Principals with mailbox-level Microsoft Graph permissions (Mail.ReadWrite, Mail.Send, MailboxSettings.ReadWrite or equivalent). These permissions allow an app to read all email in the organisation or send as any user - a high-value target for data exfiltration and business email compromise (BEC). SPNs with mailbox access and no active usage are especially concerning. Detailed emits one row per affected asset (PrimaryEntityId-keyed), suitable for ticket creation, remediation tracking, and per-asset evidence. Per-identity detail view for SPN MailboxAccess Summary.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Assign at least two owners who answer for the application (credential rotation, permission review), or remove the service principal if no one claims it.
reports.si_description: Per-row detail view for Identity_SPN_Orphan_NoOwner_Summary. Service Principals with no registered owner. Ownerless SPNs have no accountability for credential rotation, permission review, or decommissioning. Privileged orphaned SPNs are critical: no one is responsible for monitoring or revoking access. Detailed emits one row per affected asset (PrimaryEntityId-keyed), suitable for ticket creation, remediation tracking, and per-asset evidence. Per-identity detail view for SPN Orphan NoOwner Summary.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Remove the credential the application does not use; keep one (a certificate preferred) and rotate it on a schedule.
reports.si_description: Per-row detail view for Identity_SPN_OverCredentialed_Summary. Service Principals that have both a client secret AND a certificate registered. Over-credentialed SPNs increase the credential attack surface - two different authentication paths must both be managed and rotated. Often indicates legacy credentials were not cleaned up when the SPN was migrated to certificate auth. Severity: Medium (fixed). Detailed emits one row per affected asset (PrimaryEntityId-keyed), suitable for ticket creation, remediation tracking, and per-asset evidence. Per-identity detail view for SPN OverCredentialed Summary.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Remove PrivilegedAccess.ReadWrite.AzureAD from the application unless it is a governed PIM management tool.
reports.si_description: Per-row detail view for Identity_SPN_PrivilegedAccessWrite_Summary. Service Principals with PrivilegedAccess.ReadWrite.AzureAD permission. This allows the SPN to directly create, modify, or remove PIM role eligibility and assignment schedules. A compromised SPN with this permission can make any account permanently eligible for Global Administrator with no approval workflow, or remove existing PIM assignments to cover tracks. Severity: Very High (fixed) -- direct PIM manipulation capability. Detailed emits one row per affected asset (PrimaryEntityId-keyed), suitable for ticket creation, remediation tracking, and per-asset evidence. Per-identity detail view for SPN PrivilegedAccessWrite Summary.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Remove RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory from the application unless it is a governed role-management tool; grant a narrower permission instead.
reports.si_description: Per-row detail view for Identity_SPN_RoleManagementWrite_Summary. Service Principals with the RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory Graph permission. This permission allows the SPN to assign ANY Entra ID role to ANY principal, including Global Administrator. A compromised SPN with this permission can immediately elevate any account to full tenant administrator -- the equivalent of a skeleton key to the entire Entra ID tenant. This is arguably the most dangerous single Graph permission that exists. Severity: Very High (fixed). Detailed emits one row per affected asset (PrimaryEntityId-keyed), suitable for ticket creation, remediation tracking, and per-asset evidence. Per-identity detail view for SPN RoleManagementWrite Summary.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Confirm where the application comes from; remove its high permissions (or the application) if it is not trusted, and require a verified publisher for applications that get Tier 0/1 permissions.
reports.si_description: Per-row detail view for Identity_SPN_UnverifiedPublisher_HighPermission_Summary. Service Principals with Tier 0/1 permissions whose publisher has not been verified by Microsoft. Unverified publishers are anonymous -- there is no accountability for the code running in your tenant. High-privilege unverified apps represent a supply chain risk: the app developer could push malicious updates, and there is no way to validate the publisher's identity or intent. Severity: High (fixed). Detailed emits one row per affected asset (PrimaryEntityId-keyed), suitable for ticket creation, remediation tracking, and per-asset evidence. Per-identity detail view for SPN UnverifiedPublisher HighPermission Summary.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Stop interactive use of the service account: block interactive sign-in (Conditional Access or logon rights), rotate its password and give the person a personal account.
reports.si_description: Per-row detail view for Identity_ServiceAccount_InteractiveSignIn_Summary. Accounts classified by MDI as service accounts (MDI_IsServiceAccount = true) that have interactive human sign-ins recorded in SigninLogs. Service accounts should authenticate exclusively via non-interactive flows (daemon credentials, managed identity, service principal). Interactive logins indicate the service account credentials are being used by a human -- either a shared password problem, a developer using service credentials to bypass controls, or a threat actor who harvested the credentials and is performing hands-on-keyboard activity. Severity: High (fixed). Detailed emits one row per affected asset (PrimaryEntityId-keyed), suitable for ticket creation, remediation tracking, and per-asset evidence. Per-identity detail view for ServiceAccount InteractiveSignIn Summary.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Verify the sign-ins; limit the service account to trusted locations with Conditional Access and rotate its credentials if the sign-ins are unexplained.
reports.si_description: Per-row detail view for Identity_ServiceAccount_SignIn_NonTrustedLocation_Summary. Accounts classified as service accounts by MDI (MDI_IsServiceAccount = true) that have successfully authenticated from non-trusted network locations. Service accounts are expected to authenticate exclusively from known, trusted infrastructure (application servers, automation agents). Authentication from an untrusted location strongly suggests the service account credentials have been harvested and are being used by a threat actor. Severity: High (fixed). Detailed emits one row per affected asset (PrimaryEntityId-keyed), suitable for ticket creation, remediation tracking, and per-asset evidence. Per-identity detail view for ServiceAccount SignIn NonTrustedLocation Summary.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Remove the account from the on-premises privileged group (including nested membership); if the access is needed, document it and manage it through your privileged access process.
reports.si_description: Per-row detail view for Identity_ShadowAdmin_Summary. Users classified as shadow admins: they hold Tier 0/1 AD group membership (e.g. Domain Admins inherited via group nesting) but have no visible Entra ID role assignments. These accounts exercise privileged AD access that may not be tracked by standard Entra ID governance tooling, creating a blind spot in access reviews and PIM coverage. Detailed emits one row per affected asset (PrimaryEntityId-keyed), suitable for ticket creation, remediation tracking, and per-asset evidence. Per-identity detail view for ShadowAdmin Summary.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Remove the guest account, or disable it until its sponsor confirms it is needed, and run recurring access reviews for guest users.
reports.si_description: Per-row detail view for Identity_StaleGuest_NoLogin90Days_Summary. B2B guest/external collaborator accounts with no sign-in for 90+ days. Guests have a shorter stale threshold than internal users as they represent external access that should be regularly re-validated. Stale guest accounts are a common vector for supply chain and partner-related compromises. Detailed emits one row per affected asset (PrimaryEntityId-keyed), suitable for ticket creation, remediation tracking, and per-asset evidence. Per-identity detail view for StaleGuest NoLogin90Days Summary.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Reduce Global Administrators to the few who need it (Microsoft recommends fewer than five, plus break-glass accounts): move the others to least-privilege roles and make Global Administrator eligible in PIM.
reports.si_description: Per-row detail view for Identity_TooManyGlobalAdmins_Summary. Detects when the organisation has more than 5 active Global Administrator accounts. Microsoft recommends 2-5 Global Admins maximum. Each additional Global Admin increases the attack surface proportionally. Organisations with 10+ Global Admins typically have role assignment hygiene problems and lack a formal review process. Severity: High (fixed) - excessive Global Admin count is always a significant risk. Detailed emits one row per affected asset (PrimaryEntityId-keyed), suitable for ticket creation, remediation tracking, and per-asset evidence. Per-identity detail view for TooManyGlobalAdmins Summary.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Close the open port at the network edge (network security group or firewall) unless it must be public; if it must, limit the source addresses and keep the service behind it patched.
reports.si_description: Public IPs that Shodan reports with one or more open ports, aggregated per asset. Severity follows the criticality tier of the asset the IP belongs to. High-severity ports (SSH 22, RDP 3389, MSSQL 1433, MySQL 3306, PostgreSQL 5432, WinRM 5985/5986) tagged separately. Source: the public IP CI (SI_CI_CL), from the Shodan scanner.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Close the open port at the network edge (network security group or firewall) unless it must be public; if it must, limit the source addresses and keep the service behind it patched.
reports.si_description: Per-row Detailed view of public-IP open ports. Severity follows the criticality tier of the asset the IP belongs to. One row per (AssetName, IpAddress, Port). Source: the public IP CI (SI_CI_CL), from the Shodan scanner.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Update the service exposed on the public IP to a version that fixes the vulnerability, or remove its public exposure.
reports.si_description: Public IPs that Shodan reports with one or more known CVEs. A vulnerability reachable from the internet is treated as Very High severity whatever the asset tier, because the exposure itself is the risk; the tier of the owning asset then ranks the findings within that severity. Source: the public IP CI (SI_CI_CL), from the Shodan scanner.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Update the service exposed on the public IP to a version that fixes the vulnerability, or remove its public exposure.
reports.si_description: Per-row Detailed view of public-IP CVEs. Every row is Very High severity because the vulnerability is reachable from the internet. One row per (AssetName, IpAddress, CVE). Source: the public IP CI (SI_CI_CL), from the Shodan scanner.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Handle the device's open incident in Microsoft Defender: isolate the device if needed, remediate, and reset the credentials used on it.
reports.si_description: Endpoints of every tier (ranked by tier) where Microsoft Exposure Mgmt has flagged recent compromise indicators (NodeProperties.rawData.isCompromisedRecently). New v2.2 lens enabled by EG-derived IsCompromisedRecently signal (MS-computed). Aggregated per (Tier x Severity x cmdb*) bucket; lists carry impacted-asset detail.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Handle the device's open incident in Microsoft Defender: isolate the device if needed, remediate, and reset the credentials used on it.
reports.si_description: Per-asset detail view of Tier 0/1 endpoints flagged by Microsoft Exposure Mgmt as recently compromised. One row per asset.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Disable the departed person's account, revoke its sessions, remove its group memberships and roles, and delete it after your retention period.
reports.si_description: Users whose EmployeeLeaveDateTime is in the past but the account is still enabled. HR off-boarding gap; common attack path.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Remove the privileged roles and group memberships from the disabled account.
reports.si_description: Disabled account still has privileged role -- re-enable resurrects access

reports.si_fix_remediation: Remove the disabled account from the critical (privileged) groups.
reports.si_description: Disabled account still has privileged group / role -- re-enable resurrects privilege

reports.si_fix_remediation: Remove the privileged role from the guest account; if the person needs admin access, give them a member account in this tenant governed by PIM.
reports.si_description: External guest holds Entra role assignment

reports.si_fix_remediation: Convert the permanent (active) role assignment to an eligible assignment in Privileged Identity Management, with MFA, justification and a time limit on activation.
reports.si_description: Users / SPNs holding PERMANENT (always-on) privileged role assignments instead of PIM-eligible. Standing privilege violates JIT/JEA.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Bring the privileged user under Conditional Access: a policy that requires phishing-resistant MFA (and a compliant device) for admin roles, without an exclusion for this account.
reports.si_description: Privileged users whose recent successful sign-ins did NOT trigger any Conditional Access policy. Effectively bypasses CA enforcement.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Remove full mailbox access (full_access_as_app / impersonation) from the application, or scope it to the mailboxes it needs with RBAC for Applications.
reports.si_description: SPNs holding Mail.Read / Mail.Send / Mail.ReadWrite as APPLICATION permission (impersonates ANY user mailbox tenant-wide). Common path for phishing-as-a-service compromise.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Review the application's owners and remove those who should not control a privileged application (an owner can add credentials and act as the application).
reports.si_description: SPN ownership not aligned with app registration ownership

reports.si_fix_remediation: Remove public access from the resource the application controls, or reduce the application's rights on it.
reports.si_description: Service principals that hold ownership / contributor RBAC on an azure resource which is publicly exposed (IsPubliclyExposed=true) AND the SPN has stale credentials or is itself privileged. Identifies "hot" SPNs with maximum blast radius if compromised.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Review the nested membership that puts the account in a critical AD group; remove it if it is not needed and document any that stays.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Work through the account's risk factors, most severe first (missing MFA, privileged role, stale sign-in, old password); each one removed lowers the account's risk.
reports.si_description: Identities with 4+ risk factors flagged. Above the I16 threshold (3+) -- these are the worst offenders.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Disable the departed person's account, revoke its sessions, remove its group memberships and roles, and delete it after your retention period.
reports.si_description: Users whose EmployeeLeaveDateTime is in the past but the account is still enabled. HR off-boarding gap; common attack path. Summary emits one row per finding type (Category x Subcategory x ConfigurationName), with AssetCount/TotalIssues/ImpactedAssets aggregated -- suitable for dashboards and exec reporting.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Remove the privileged roles and group memberships from the disabled account.
reports.si_description: Identities flagged DisabledPrivilegedUser by the engine -- account disabled but still carries privileged role assignment. Summary emits one row per finding type (Category x Subcategory x ConfigurationName), with AssetCount/TotalIssues/ImpactedAssets aggregated -- suitable for dashboards and exec reporting.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Remove the disabled account from the critical (privileged) groups.
reports.si_description: Disabled users still in critical AD nested groups OR with active Entra roles. Cleanup gap; account re-enable would resurrect privilege. Summary emits one row per finding type (Category x Subcategory x ConfigurationName), with AssetCount/TotalIssues/ImpactedAssets aggregated -- suitable for dashboards and exec reporting.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Remove the privileged role from the guest account; if the person needs admin access, give them a member account in this tenant governed by PIM.

Summary emits one row per finding type (Category x Subcategory x ConfigurationName), with AssetCount/TotalIssues/ImpactedAssets aggregated -- suitable for dashboards and exec reporting.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Convert the permanent (active) role assignment to an eligible assignment in Privileged Identity Management, with MFA, justification and a time limit on activation.
reports.si_description: Users / SPNs holding PERMANENT (always-on) privileged role assignments instead of PIM-eligible. Standing privilege violates JIT/JEA. Summary emits one row per finding type (Category x Subcategory x ConfigurationName), with AssetCount/TotalIssues/ImpactedAssets aggregated -- suitable for dashboards and exec reporting.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Bring the privileged user under Conditional Access: a policy that requires phishing-resistant MFA (and a compliant device) for admin roles, without an exclusion for this account.
reports.si_description: Privileged users whose recent successful sign-ins did NOT trigger any Conditional Access policy. Effectively bypasses CA enforcement. Summary emits one row per finding type (Category x Subcategory x ConfigurationName), with AssetCount/TotalIssues/ImpactedAssets aggregated -- suitable for dashboards and exec reporting.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Remove full mailbox access (full_access_as_app / impersonation) from the application, or scope it to the mailboxes it needs with RBAC for Applications.
reports.si_description: SPNs holding Mail.Read / Mail.Send / Mail.ReadWrite as APPLICATION permission (impersonates ANY user mailbox tenant-wide). Common path for phishing-as-a-service compromise. Summary emits one row per finding type (Category x Subcategory x ConfigurationName), with AssetCount/TotalIssues/ImpactedAssets aggregated -- suitable for dashboards and exec reporting.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Review the application's owners and remove those who should not control a privileged application (an owner can add credentials and act as the application).
reports.si_description: SPNs whose Owner is different from the Application Owner -- common in apps inherited from a departed employee where ownership got cleaned up only on one side. Summary emits one row per finding type (Category x Subcategory x ConfigurationName), with AssetCount/TotalIssues/ImpactedAssets aggregated -- suitable for dashboards and exec reporting.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Check why the device is excluded from Microsoft Defender; remove the exclusion if it no longer applies so the device is assessed again.
reports.si_description: Every endpoint currently suppressed from Risk Analysis by an operator exclusion tag, and the exact tag that did it. This is the INVERSE of every other report -- it deliberately does not filter excluded assets out, because they are the subject. Exclusion was previously invisible - a tagged asset simply vanished from every report with nothing recording that it had been dropped or why, which an operator cannot tell apart from collection having broken. Severity follows the asset's own criticality tier, so a suppressed Tier 0 asset surfaces at the top - suppressing a critical asset is the governance risk worth reviewing, and a stale exclusion tag never expires on its own.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Check why the device is excluded from Microsoft Defender; remove the exclusion if it no longer applies so the device is assessed again.
reports.si_description: How many endpoints are currently suppressed from Risk Analysis by an operator exclusion tag, grouped by criticality tier, with the assets and the exact tags listed. The Summary answers "how much of the estate am I not looking at, and is any of it critical"; the Detailed pair lists it asset by asset. Exclusion was previously invisible - a tagged asset simply vanished from every report with nothing recording that it had been dropped or why. Severity follows the asset's own tier, so suppressed Tier 0 assets sort to the top - exclusion tags never expire, and a critical asset suppressed by a tag added months ago is a governance gap rather than a preference.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Keep one tier tag on the device: remove the conflicting tier tags in Microsoft Defender, or set the tier in SecurityInsight.
reports.si_description: Every endpoint whose operator tags assert TWO OR MORE different criticality tiers at once, with the exact conflicting tags. Tier is computed as a MIN across all signals, so the most critical tag silently wins and nothing breaks - which is precisely why this has never been visible. The estate can assert that one machine is both Tier 0 and Tier 3 and no report says so. Measured on a live estate, 16 of 19 tagged endpoints carried contradictory tier tags, including a privileged-access workstation tagged both PAWDevices tier 0 and EmployeeWorkstations tier 3, and a domain controller whose certificate-services tag claimed tier 0 and tier 1 simultaneously. Severity follows the MOST critical tier claimed, because a conflict involving a Tier 0 claim is the one where being wrong costs the most.

reports.si_fix_remediation: Keep one tier tag on the device: remove the conflicting tier tags in Microsoft Defender, or set the tier in SecurityInsight.
reports.si_description: How many endpoints carry operator tags that assert more than one criticality tier, grouped by the most critical tier claimed, with the assets listed. The Summary answers "how much of my tagging disagrees with itself"; the Detailed pair names the tags per asset. Because tier is a MIN, a conflict never fails - the most critical tag wins and the estate looks healthy, so the only way to see this is to ask. A cluster of assets sharing one conflicting pair usually means a tagging rule was changed and the old tag was never removed, which is a single fix rather than one per machine.
